title: Augment Code Pricing 2026: Plans, Credits & Costs
summary: Augment code pricing charges $20 or $100 monthly, but the real cost depends on your usage—compare plans by credits spent per task, not the monthly fee.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


### Is there a free plan or free trial for Augment Code?


We didn't confirm a free plan or trial as of this article's check date, so don't build a budget around one. Trial terms are where vendors change the most, and a trial's credit allowance may be sized differently from a paid plan's.


Burn rate measured on a trial can understate what a paid month costs. Read the current pricing page, and if a trial exists, log your credits per task during it anyway.


### Do unused Augment Code credits roll over?


Treat unused credits as expiring unless the vendor's pricing page or your account terms say otherwise. We didn't verify a rollover policy, and this is the clause worth reading line by line.


If credits reset each cycle, a plan sized for your busiest week wastes money in quiet weeks. If they carry over, a larger allowance costs less than it looks. Ask support in writing and keep the reply.


### Can I switch plans mid-month without losing credits?


Whether a mid-cycle switch preserves, prorates or resets your credits isn't something we could confirm, so find out before you switch, not after.


The risk is concrete: an upgrade made after you run dry could replace your remaining balance, or start a fresh allowance, depending on how billing handles it. Get the behavior in a support reply, and switch at a cycle boundary when you can.


### Is Augment Code cheaper for teams than for individuals?


Not necessarily. We didn't confirm that team pricing is cheaper per seat, and the answer depends on whether credits are pooled or per person.


Pooled credits let a light user's unused allowance cover a heavy user's spike. Per-seat credits mean your heaviest agent user still hits a wall while others leave allowance unused. Compare credits per task across your actual team members, not the per-seat headline.


### How do I know when Augment Code has changed its prices again?


Assume the pricing page can change without notice, and re-check it against your logged burn on a schedule.


Compare three things each time: the credit allowance, the credit cost of the actions you run most, and any change to overage or rollover terms. A headline price that stays put can hide a changed credit rate.


Save a dated copy of the page when you subscribe, so you have something to hold up if a support ticket claims nothing's changed. Also watch your billing email, since account notices can arrive before the public page is updated.
